Load balancing, DNS, edge

Route, balance, and accelerate traffic across the globe.

1. Core Concept

  • Route 53 maps names to IPs. CloudFront caches at the edge. Load Balancers distribute traffic to healthy compute targets. Global Accelerator optimizes paths over the AWS backbone.

2. Key Services & Features

  • Route 53:
    • DNS service with routing policies (Latency, Geolocation, Failover).
    • Alias records connect apex domains (example.com) to AWS resources for free.
  • CloudFront:
    • Global CDN.
    • Caches static and dynamic HTTP content.
    • Uses Origin Access Control (OAC) to secure S3 origins.
  • Application Load Balancer (ALB):
    • Layer 7 (HTTP/HTTPS).
    • Routes based on URL path, host, or headers.
    • Targets EC2, ECS, Lambda.
  • Network Load Balancer (NLB):
    • Layer 4 (TCP/UDP).
    • Ultra-low latency, handles millions of requests.
    • Provides a Static IP per AZ.
  • Global Accelerator:
    • Provides 2 static Anycast IPs.
    • Routes non-HTTP and HTTP traffic over the AWS backbone to the nearest healthy region.
    • Sub-second failover.

3. Architecture Rules

  • For cross-region active-passive disaster recovery, use Route 53 Failover Routing with Health Checks.
  • If a client requires a static whitelist IP but you need load balancing, you must use an NLB.

4. Scenarios & Use Cases

  • API requests to /users must go to one target group, and /orders to another.
    • Choose: Application Load Balancer (ALB).
    • Why: It is the only load balancer that inspects Layer 7 HTTP paths.
  • A global gaming app using UDP requires ultra-fast multi-region failover.
    • Choose: AWS Global Accelerator.
    • Why: It supports UDP, bypasses DNS TTL limits, and uses the optimized AWS network.

  • B Automatic data replication across all Regions
